payload.title: Wedding Flowers in Season in Australia by Month
protect_keywords: in season or imported wedding flowers
fashionable flowers opt for in-season or order imported (old title)
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a generous budget and a date (or a shortlist of dates) in mind, at home or overseas, who want to know which flowers are naturally in season in their wedding month, whether a bloom they love will need to be imported, and what to ask their florist so the look they picture is realistic for the season and the place.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning the wedding (single primary CTA in the close, after the destination weddings and planning sections).
payload.angle: Most in-season flower lists are written for the northern hemisphere or list blooms with no source. This is the Australian hub: twelve short month notes that name only flowers a source supports for that month (anything unsourced becomes 'ask your florist'), each linking our deeper monthly post where one exists, then a plain answer to the old question of in season or imported, grounded in the fact that imported cut flowers must meet Australian biosecurity import conditions, and practical guidance for destination couples whose season follows the destination, not home.
must_include: Intro (short, no year), then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways
H2 'Why season matters for wedding flowers': advice only (freshness, availability, how season shapes the look), no statistics or claims of environmental impact unless sourced

H2 month by month for Australia: say plainly that Australia's seasons run opposite to the northern hemisphere (summer is December to February); then 12 H3s, January to December, each a short note listing only flowers a cited source supports for that month in Australia; where no source supports a pairing write 'ask your florist'; link the month's live in-season post where one exists (SEO step supplies the six live monthly URLs, including spring, July, August, November and December)

H2 'In season or imported?': keep the old post's question; state that imported cut flowers must meet Australian biosecurity import conditions, as the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry states, linked at the claim [[VERIFY]]; then advise asking the florist which stems are local, which are imported and what the backup is
H2 destination weddings: flower seasons follow the destination, not Australia; ask a local florist at the destination what is in season for the date
H2 planning: when to talk to your florist about substitutes and backups (as advice, no fixed week counts presented as rules); link /style-advice/wedding-flowers-cost with no figures
FAQ (4 to 6 questions; no prices, no statistics, no 'best')

Close with one Wedded Advisor line using confirmed claims only from brand-facts.md (one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact; plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world), linking /wonderland-concierge
Internal links: each live monthly in-season post (URLs from SEO), /style-advice/wedding-flowers-cost, /wonderland-concierge
